item.title: New RPG Is Basically Fallout Meets Fishing Trip from Hell, and You’re Bait
item.description:
Horror-fishing RPG Dreadmoor is finally preparing to set sail, with its November 9 launch just 24 hours away as of this writing. While its early access launch has been eight years in the making, developer Dream Dock appears confident that the biggest hurdles are now behind the project, estimating that Dreadmoor will reach version 1.0 within six to 12 months.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

Dreadmoor is an action-horror RPG from Kyrgyzstan-based developer Dream Dock and Cyprus-based publisher Digital Vortex Entertainment. Set in the Submerged Lands, a post-apocalyptic region of flooded settlements, crumbling infrastructure, and mutated wildlife, the game puts players in command of a fishing trawler traveling between isolated communities and trading catches for supplies. Reminiscent of the desolate landscape of The Island from Fallout 4 's Far Harbor DLC, the region has been transformed by a mysterious biological threat known as the Sea Blight.

Best Horror Games Set At Sea, Ranked

The ocean can be an incredibly terrifying thing to some. Here are some of the best horror games that are set at sea, ranked.

By Allison Stalberg

Fishing in Dreadmoor Can Be Deadly

In More Ways than One, to Put It Mildly

Fishing forms the backbone of Dreadmoor 's survival mechanics and, consequently, its core gameplay loop. Players must constantly search for productive fishing grounds, select appropriate bait, and reel in valuable species, many of which have mutated in disturbing ways. Some cause trouble even after capture, since creatures stored together in the trawler’s hold may devour one another. Larger predators pose a far greater danger, potentially turning a routine expedition into a fight to avoid becoming their next meal. Combined with ruined coastal communities, hostile mutations, and an oppressive atmosphere, Dreadmoor kind of has the vibe of a survival RPG from the perspective of Fallout 4: Far Harbor 's fishermen.

Wishlist Today

Its gameplay differs considerably, however, with the emphasis on navigating hazardous waters and confronting Lovecraftian creatures beneath the surface making it more reminiscent of a post-apocalyptic, fishing-focused Subnautica . The similarities extend to exploration and resource gathering, as players can supplement their fishing income by scavenging abandoned buildings, caves, and shipwrecks for scrap metal, blueprints, and other valuables. Recovered materials can be used to craft specialized lures, reinforced harpoons, medicine, and survival gear, while the trawler itself can be upgraded with improved engines, hull reinforcement, and lighting. This combination of exploration, crafting, and survival mechanics gives Dreadmoor a more varied gameplay loop than its horror-fishing label might suggest.

Two iconic game characters. One impossible mashup.
Can you name them both?

The game’s Lovecraftian influences emerge through its grotesque creatures and the Sea Blight, which has transformed much of the local wildlife. Traveling after dark adds hazards, making the timing of expeditions another survival factor to consider. Like the terrifying sea monsters encountered in Dredge , these threats make the waterways themselves highly unpredictable. Unlike that acclaimed fishing-horror hybrid, however, Dreadmoor raises the stakes with real-time combat, allowing players to confront hostile creatures at sea or on land, and sometimes even requiring them to do both as part of a single encounter if a particularly cranky critter ends up pursuing them ashore.

What to Expect From Dreadmoor’s Early Access Release

Dreadmoor will enter Steam Early Access with one major explorable region, its complete core gameplay loop, and a story campaign with a defined ending. Players can continue fishing, exploring, collecting rare specimens, and upgrading equipment after completing the campaign. Dream Dock has set the launch price at $19.99 in the U.S. and €20.49 in Germany, with an optional Supporter Pack priced at $4.99 and €4.89, respectively. The 12 languages will be supported at launch, including English, Spanish, French, and German, as well as Japanese, Korean, and Chinese—both Simplified and Traditional. Publisher Digital Vortex Entertainment plans to raise the game's price after version 1.0 arrives, which is currently estimated to happen sometime between mid-2027 and late 2027 or early 2028.

item.description:
Choosing the right race and lineage in Beyond Nen gives you powerful permanent boosts that help in every fight and adventure. The top options include Celestial, with its Strength, Weapon, Durability, Nen, Stamina, and extra Damage boosts, plus rare lineages like Zoldyck that increase money gain and add strong combat modes. Having the best race and lineage makes hard bosses easier and helps you progress faster through the Hunter x Hunter -inspired world.

Best Races and Lineages in Beyond Nen, Explained

Celestial is the strongest race for most players thanks to a +5% boost to Strength, Weapon, Durability, Nen, and Stamina, which stacks with everything you do, and the extra damage helps finish fights quicker. Rolling a high-tier race and lineage together creates the strongest possible start in Beyond Nen .

item.title: Destiny 2's Unvaulting Plan Quietly Pushes Any Real Sequel Further Away Than Fans Think
item.description:
When Bungie announced back in May that Destiny 2 was coming to the end of its live-service support, I couldn't help but feel like a pretty significant part of my gaming history was coming to an end. I've played Destiny 2 off and on for years, sometimes stepping away for extended periods before eventually finding myself drawn back into its world, and I even wrote about what the announcement meant to me at the time. But as difficult as it was to accept that Bungie was moving on, I also understood that whatever came next for Destiny was going to take years to develop, especially since the studio had only just announced its intentions to begin incubating new projects. Unfortunately, Bungie's recent decision to bring much of Destiny 2 's vaulted content back has made the road to that eventual successor look considerably longer than I initially expected.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

Now, obviously, I don't think anyone was expecting Destiny 3 to launch anytime soon, if at all, especially considering Bungie only released Destiny 2 's supposed final content update in June. However, the studio's October 29 community update revealed that its plans to restore the game's missing campaigns and activities won't be completed until early 2028 at the soonest, assuming development goes according to plan. That's more than a year away, and Bungie has made it clear that restoring the original experience is only the beginning of its larger vision for the franchise. Considering how early that vision apparently is, I'm beginning to wonder just how long Destiny 2 will need to keep players entertained before Bungie has something genuinely new to show them.

Destiny 2 Is Taking the Right First Step, but Bungie's Biggest Challenge Is What Comes Next

Bungie's Destiny 2 unvaulting strategy is a good one, but in order to rebuild more than trust, the Destiny franchise needs to head toward the future.

By Christopher Adams

Destiny 2's Comeback Has a 2028 Catch

For those who haven't followed Bungie's plans to restore Destiny 2 , the studio is currently working to bring back the Red War, Curse of Osiris, Warmind, and Forsaken campaigns, all of which were removed from the game years ago. The restoration will also include associated Strikes, Raids, and Raid Lairs, along with the Menagerie activity from Season of Opulence, complete with reprised rewards. It's an enormous amount of content, and considering how much of Destiny 2 's original story has been inaccessible since Bungie introduced the Destiny Content Vault in 2020, I can understand why the studio is making its return a priority. As someone who experienced those early campaigns when they were still available, I'd certainly welcome the opportunity to revisit them.

Unfortunately, bringing all that content back is going to take quite a bit of work, which Bungie previously explained in its September announcement. According to the developer, changes made to Destiny 2 since Beyond Light mean that older activities require substantial updates to lighting, enemy encounters, and other underlying systems before they can function properly again. The October update revealed that the project is expected to remain in pre-production until January or February 2027, followed by approximately 12 months of full production to complete the porting process. That puts the estimated finish line in early 2028, although it's worth mentioning that Bungie hasn't confirmed when all that restored content will actually be released.

What interests me most about the announcement, however, is Bungie's reasoning for prioritizing the restoration in the first place. Head of product Josh Deane acknowledged that removing essential parts of Destiny 2 damaged the relationship between Bungie and its community, arguing that the franchise needs to regain that trust before it can confidently move forward. I actually agree with him there, especially considering how difficult it is to recommend a story-driven game to someone when several of its most important chapters are missing entirely. But fixing that mistake is apparently going to occupy a substantial part of Destiny 's immediate future, and I imagine Bungie understands that bringing back old content won't automatically convince everyone to stick around until something new arrives.

I'm beginning to wonder just how long Destiny 2 will need to keep players entertained before Bungie has something genuinely new to show them.

Bungie also outlined several other projects in its October update, including a planned Destiny 2 Celebration, something called Destiny Legacy, and another initiative the studio isn't ready to discuss. Those projects are being developed as part of a broader plan for the franchise, but Deane acknowledged that Bungie is still in the process of incubating and validating its more ambitious ideas before committing larger teams to them. None of that means a sequel can't be developed alongside the restoration, of course, and Bungie hasn't indicated that work on a future Destiny game has to wait until 2028. However, with no sequel announced and the studio still determining what its next major projects should look like, I wouldn't expect the franchise's next chapter to be anywhere close to ready by the time Destiny 2 's missing content has been restored.

Destiny 2's Future Depends on How Long Its Past Can Keep Players Around

As excited as I am about the possibility of revisiting some of Destiny 2 's earliest campaigns, I also have to admit that I'm a little concerned about how much Bungie is relying on nostalgia to carry the game through this transition. I've returned to Destiny 2 more times than I can count over the years, but usually because there was something I hadn't experienced yet. Revisiting the Red War and Forsaken will certainly be enjoyable, especially after being unable to play them properly for so long, but I can't imagine that excitement lasting indefinitely. And with some additional content, including free-roam destinations and seasonal activities, still being considered rather than guaranteed, the restoration might not even bring back everything longtime players remember.

Destiny 2 Officially Gets New Content Timeline

Still, I don't want to overlook how significant this decision could be for Destiny 's future, particularly if Bungie genuinely intends to make its universe whole again before introducing the next major installment. A sequel was always going to be years away after the studio effectively brought Destiny 2 's ongoing development to an end, but the unvaulting initiative has given us a much clearer idea of what those intervening years are going to look like. Bungie is essentially betting that restoring the experiences players fell in love with will give them enough reason to return while the studio works toward whatever comes next, and I sincerely hope that bet pays off. Destiny 2 has been part of my gaming life for far too long for me to want anything other than a successful comeback, but if its future is going to depend so heavily on revisiting the past, Bungie has quite a bit to prove before I'm convinced this new beginning will last.

item.title: New Co-Op PvE Game Officially Confirmed for PS5
item.description:
Developer Keepsake Games has confirmed that Jump Space , a co-op PvE space shooter, is coming to PlayStation 5 soon. Formerly known as Jump Ship , the game has been available on PC via Steam since 2025 and has earned around 86% positive player reviews as of this writing. Jump Space remains in early access, and Keepsake Games appears to be planning its PlayStation 5 release before the game's 1.0 launch.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

Jump Space 's PS5 announcement may come as a surprise to fans of sci-fi co-op games, as Keepsake Games previously said that the console port would launch alongside the game's 1.0 release. More specifically, the team said, "For now, you can assume that early access and these content updates will continue for all of 2027, with PS5 and crossplay coming once we hit 1.0." However, plans appear to have changed, and PS5 players may get to enjoy the game much sooner than expected.

New Open-World Cozy Game Coming to PS5 on November 17

PlayStation 5 is set to receive a brand-new open-world cozy game on November 17, and it already has plenty of positive user reviews.

By Mohsen Baqery

Jump Space Is Coming to PS5 in Q1 2027

item.title: Pokopia Just Did Something for Switch 2 That Pokemon Winds and Waves Now Has to Match
item.description:
Pokemon Pokopia has already achieved something Nintendo now expects from Pokemon Winds and Waves : convincing people to buy a Nintendo Switch 2. During Nintendo's November 2026 financial-results briefing, company president Shuntaro Furukawa confirmed that the cozy Pokemon spin-off had been a major driver of hardware sales. Furukawa also described the upcoming mainline Pokemon games as a crucial release for the console as it enters its third year on the market.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

That's an impressive accomplishment for a game that takes such a different approach to the usual formula. Rather than focusing on becoming a Pokemon Champion, Pokemon Pokopia gives players a world to rebuild alongside their favorite creatures—likely inspired by the success of Animal Crossing: New Horizons . Its success has demonstrated that an unconventional Pokemon experience can help sell Nintendo's newest console. With Pokemon Winds and Waves scheduled for 2027, the next generation of Pokemon games now has a high standard to meet.

It's Officially a New Era for the Nintendo Switch 2

With the recent release of Pokemon Pokopia, the official Pokemon on Nintendo Switch 2 era has begun in earnest for fans and players.

By Joshua Duckworth

Pokemon Pokopia Has Already Proven It Can Sell Switch 2 Consoles

When Pokemon Pokopia launched exclusively for Switch 2 on March 5, 2026, it represented a bold departure for the franchise. Players take control of a Ditto that has transformed into a human, restoring a neglected world by creating habitats and building homes for Pokemon. It's a much more relaxed experience than the traditional Pokemon RPGs, with its appeal coming from watching a once-empty environment gradually become populated. That approach clearly resonated with players. Pokemon Pokopia sold more than 2.2 million copies worldwide in its first four days, surpassed 4 million in five weeks, and reached over 5 million within its first four months. Those are impressive numbers for a spin-off that offers such a departure from the mainline series, especially considering it was released exclusively for a console that had been available for less than a year.

The more interesting part of Pokemon Pokopia's success, however, is what Nintendo has said about its impact on hardware sales. During the company's May 2026 financial briefing, Furukawa credited the game with driving Switch 2 purchases and expressed hope that it would become an evergreen title with a long sales life. His November 2026 comments reinforced that assessment, confirming that Pokemon Pokopia had helped sustain the console's sales momentum. That's the most remarkable part of the whole situation. A Pokemon game built around taking things slowly has become an important part of Nintendo's efforts to move players onto its newest hardware.

A Pokemon game built around taking things slowly has become an important part of Nintendo's efforts to move players onto its newest hardware.

Pokemon Winds and Waves face greater expectations as the next mainline entries in one of gaming's most successful franchises. Their 2027 release will take players into a new open-world setting featuring windswept islands and a vast ocean, offering a different environment from previous Pokemon adventures. The initial announcement has already given fans a glimpse of the new region, along with its starter Pokemon, setting the stage for another major evolution of the series. As Switch 2 exclusives, both games also have the responsibility of demonstrating what Pokemon can accomplish on Nintendo's newer hardware. For players still using the original Switch, the new generation represents one of the strongest reasons to finally upgrade.

As of September 30, 2026, Pokemon Scarlet and Violet had sold 28.66 million copies worldwide, while Pokemon Sword and Shield had reached 27.36 million. Those figures comfortably exceed Pokopia's reported sales, but the upcoming games face a different challenge. Both previous generations launched on the original Switch, whereas Winds and Waves will arrive when Nintendo is trying to encourage more existing Switch owners to make the transition. The console's September 2026 price increase adds another obstacle, with its US retail price rising from $449.99 to $499.99. At that price, convincing someone to purchase new hardware requires an especially appealing game. Pokemon Winds and Waves have the advantage of being long-awaited mainline entries, but they'll need to make the upgrade feel worthwhile.

Pokemon Winds and Waves Need to Build on Pokopia's Success

Pokemon Winds and Waves don't need to borrow Pokopia's gameplay to match its impact. The two experiences appeal to different interests, and there is already a substantial audience waiting for another traditional Pokemon adventure. What they can take from Pokopia , though, is the importance of offering an experience that justifies purchasing new hardware. For Winds and Waves , that means delivering a memorable new region and making the most of Switch 2's capabilities. The tropical environments revealed so far provide a strong foundation, but the games' real test will be how effectively they build upon the Pokemon formula.

What to Read Next
Pokemon Pokopia Is Quietly Taking a Bigger Risk With Its Next DLC
Pokemon Pokopia DLC 2 Release Date Officially Confirmed
Pokemon Pokopia DLC 2 Release Date Officially Confirmed

With the original Switch having already hosted two enormously successful mainline Pokemon generations, the next pair now has the responsibility of persuading those players that the franchise's future is worth investing in. Pokemon Pokopia has already demonstrated the influence a Switch 2-exclusive Pokemon game can have on hardware adoption, despite abandoning many of the mechanics that made the franchise famous. Winds and Waves are arriving with a much larger established audience and the weight of an entirely new generation behind them. Their success will be measured in software sales, but their ability to convince more players to leave the original Switch behind is what will make them especially valuable to Nintendo.
